description: Twenty authored gameplay scenarios. Expected answers and rubrics are evaluation-only and are never sent to the answering model.

messages.content: Can I respond to my opponent tapping a basic Forest for mana?

cases.expected_answer: No. The activated mana ability resolves immediately without using the stack.

criteria.description: Says the mana ability cannot be responded to.
Explains that the ability does not use the stack and resolves immediately.

messages.content: I have priority and cast an instant. Do I get priority again before my opponent, and does the instant resolve immediately?

cases.expected_answer: The caster receives priority again. The instant resolves only after all players pass in succession.

criteria.description: Says the caster receives priority again.
Says the instant waits for all players to pass, rather than resolving immediately.

messages.content: I cast Defiant Strike targeting my creature. My opponent destroys that creature in response. Do I still draw a card when Defiant Strike would resolve?

cases.expected_answer: No. Its only target is illegal, so the entire spell does not resolve, including the draw.

criteria.description: Says no card is drawn.
Explains that all targets are illegal and the entire spell fails to resolve.

messages.content: An instant says "Deal 2 damage to each of up to two target creatures." I choose two targets. Before it resolves, one target leaves the battlefield; the other remains legal. Does the remaining creature take 2 damage?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. The spell resolves and affects the remaining legal target; it does not affect the illegal target.

criteria.description: Says the remaining legal target takes 2 damage.
Explains that one illegal target does not stop the whole spell if another target is still legal.

messages.content: My attacking 6/6 with trample is blocked only by an undamaged 2/2 with indestructible. No other effects apply. May I assign 2 to the blocker and 4 to the defending player?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. Assigning lethal damage uses toughness and marked damage; indestructible stops destruction, not this assignment.

criteria.description: Allows the 2/4 assignment.
Explains why indestructible does not require assigning all 6 damage to the blocker.

messages.content: My attacking 5/5 has deathtouch and trample. It is blocked only by an undamaged 8/8 with no abilities. No other effects apply. What is the maximum damage I can assign to the defending player?

cases.expected_answer: 4. One damage assigned to the blocker is lethal for trample because the attacker has deathtouch.

criteria.description: Gives a maximum of 4 damage to the player.
Explains the one damage assigned to the blocker counts as lethal because of deathtouch.

messages.content: An indestructible 3/3 gets -3/-3 until end of turn. No other effects apply. Does it survive because it is indestructible?

cases.expected_answer: No. At 0 toughness it is put in its owner's graveyard as a state-based action; this is not destruction.

criteria.description: Says it goes to the graveyard.
Distinguishes zero-toughness state-based action from destruction.

messages.content: My commander is destroyed and goes from the battlefield to the graveyard. No replacement effects apply. Can I move it to the command zone, and do abilities that trigger when it dies still trigger?

cases.expected_answer: Yes to both. It died on entering the graveyard; the optional command-zone move is a subsequent state-based action.

criteria.description: Allows moving it to the command zone as a state-based action.
Says dies abilities still trigger because it reached the graveyard.

messages.content: I have cast my commander twice from the command zone and once from my hand this game. It is now in the command zone again. With no cost modifiers, how much additional commander tax applies to my next cast from there?

cases.expected_answer: An additional {4}. Only the two previous casts from the command zone count.

criteria.description: Gives additional tax of 4 generic mana.
Excludes the cast from hand when counting previous command-zone casts.

messages.content: Rest in Peace and my Blood Artist are on the battlefield. Another creature would be destroyed. With no other relevant effects, does Blood Artist trigger for that creature?

cases.expected_answer: No. Rest in Peace replaces the graveyard move with exile, so the creature does not die.

criteria.description: Says Blood Artist does not trigger for that creature.
Explains that exile replaces entering the graveyard, so no dies event occurs.

messages.content: I control Doubling Season and Anointed Procession. An effect would create one creature token under my control. No other effects apply. How many tokens do I create, and do the doublers loop forever?

cases.expected_answer: Four tokens. Each replacement effect applies once to the event; they do not loop.

criteria.description: Gives 4 tokens.
Explains each doubler applies once and there is no infinite loop.

messages.content: A source would deal 3 damage to me. Two ordinary replacement effects apply: one doubles that damage, and the other increases it by 1. Neither is a self-replacement or prevention effect and no other effects apply. Who chooses their order, and can the final damage be 7 or 8?

cases.expected_answer: The affected player (me) chooses. Double then add one gives 7; add one then double gives 8.

criteria.description: Identifies the affected player as the chooser.
Correctly describes both orders producing 7 or 8 damage.

messages.content: In a two-player game it is Alice's turn. One ordinary triggered ability Alice controls and one Bob controls trigger simultaneously. Neither triggers from another ability triggering. With no further responses, whose trigger resolves first?

cases.expected_answer: Bob's. Alice puts hers on the stack first as the active player; Bob puts his above it.

criteria.description: Says Bob's trigger resolves first.
Explains active-player/nonactive-player stacking order and last-in-first-out resolution.

messages.content: I control a printed 4/4 creature, Humility, and Glorious Anthem. The creature has no counters or other effects. What is its power/toughness? Does it matter which enchantment entered first?

cases.expected_answer: 2/2 regardless of entry order. Humility sets base P/T to 1/1 in 7b; Anthem modifies it by +1/+1 in 7c.

criteria.description: Gives 2/2.
Explains that base-setting precedes the +1/+1 modifier regardless of these enchantments' timestamps.

messages.content: I control a creature with hexproof. May I target it with my own Giant Growth, assuming I can pay for the spell and have priority?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. Hexproof only prevents targeting by opponents' spells and abilities.

criteria.description: Allows targeting one's own creature.
Explains that hexproof restricts opponents, not the creature's controller.

messages.content: My attacking 3/3 has double strike but not trample. Its only blocker is an undamaged 2/2 with no abilities. The blocker dies in the first combat damage step. Does my attacker then deal 3 damage to the player in the second combat damage step?

cases.expected_answer: No. It remains blocked and has no blocker to assign damage to; without trample it deals no damage to the defending player.

criteria.description: Says no damage is dealt to the player in the second step.
Explains the creature remains blocked and lacks trample.

messages.content: An effect exiles my creature token and then immediately tries to return it to the battlefield during the same resolution. No replacement effects apply. Does the token return?

cases.expected_answer: No. A token that has left the battlefield cannot change zones again; it later ceases to exist as a state-based action.

criteria.description: Says the token does not return.
Explains it cannot change zones again even before state-based actions, rather than claiming state-based actions interrupt resolution.

messages.content: A creature I just cast has "Sacrifice this creature: Draw a card." There is no tap or untap symbol in that cost and no other restriction. When I have priority, can I activate it this turn despite summoning sickness?

cases.expected_answer: Yes. Summoning sickness restricts attacking and creature abilities with tap/untap symbols, not this sacrifice ability.

criteria.description: Allows activating the sacrifice ability.
Explains the absence of a tap/untap symbol means summoning sickness does not prohibit it.

messages.content: I control two legendary creatures with the same name after a spell resolves. No effect changes the legend rule. Can I respond to the legend rule by casting an instant before choosing one to keep?

cases.expected_answer: No. The legend rule is a state-based action applied before anyone gets priority; choose one and put the other in its owner's graveyard.

criteria.description: Says one cannot respond with an instant before applying the legend rule.
Explains state-based actions happen before priority and one legendary permanent is kept.

messages.content: My creature has protection and my opponent used a removal spell. Is my creature safe?

cases.expected_answer: Insufficient information. Ask which creature/protection quality and which removal spell, and whether targeting or damage is involved. Do not give an unconditional yes or no.

criteria.description: Asks for the relevant protection quality and the removal spell or exact card names.
Avoids an unconditional ruling that protection always stops removal or never does.
